title: introduce-traffic-hydrator-controller-with-slo-aware-fallback-playbook
author: Marina Lopez
description:
Motivation:
Many deployments at Redwood use staged canaries, A/B experiments, or shadow validation. We observed a recurring pattern where abrupt traffic increases during promote phases spike latencies or push dependent backends to transient errors, causing noisy rollouts and manual rollbacks. This PR introduces the Traffic Hydrator controller: a light orchestration layer that smooths traffic transitions, enforces SLO-aware gating, and wires automated rollback/playbook actions when gates breach.

What this PR does (single-summary):
- Adds a new controller (traffic-hydrator) that accepts rollout intents (canary/A-B/promote) and issues fine-grained traffic change plans (micro-steps) to the routing layer.
- Integrates SLO gates (latency P95, error-rate, backend saturation) with configurable windowing and confidence thresholds.
- Exposes per-rollout telemetry: planned vs actual traffic, gate signals, and anomaly reason codes.
- Implements an automated fallback playbook: when the SLO gate is violated repeatedly within a fast-fail horizon, the controller triggers a graceful rollback, shadow-quarantine, or scaled-back slow-path depending on policy.
- Backwards compatible: the controller is opt-in per-rollout via rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled (defaults to false). Existing rollouts behave unchanged until teams opt in.

Design notes and rationale:
- Micro-step approach: instead of a single large traffic delta, we apply small fractional increments with inter-step observation windows to surface regressions early without causing large SLO regressions.
- SLO-aware thresholds: thresholds can be absolute (e.g., p95 < 120ms) or relative to baseline (e.g., p95 <= 1.25x baseline), supporting both strict and adaptive policies.
- Failure-mode policy matrix: when a gate trips we consult rollout.policy.hydrator.fail_action which can be: pause-and-alert, rollback, shadow-quarantine (route affected cohorts to shadow), or slow-path (force quantized/low-cost variant).
- Observability: new metrics (hydrator.step_duration_seconds, hydrator.step_success_total, hydrator.gate_violations_total) and trace spans for step decisions. We added Dashboard templates for rollout observers.

Files changed (high level):
- controller/traffic_hydrator/*: core controller and reconciler loop.
- api/v1/rollout_policy.proto: new hydrator policy fields and enums.
- routing/runtime_adapter.go: new smooth-apply API surface to accept micro-step plans.
- telemetry/dashboards/rollout_hydrator.json: dashboard for SREs and release owners.
- docs/runbooks/hydrator-playbook.md: human-readable playbook for incidents and manual overrides.
- tests/integration/rollout_hydrator_e2e_test.go: integration scenarios (canary success, gate-failure -> rollback, shadow-quarantine).

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Ship controller disabled by default (feature flag).
2) Early adopter opt-in: add rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled = true to a small set of internal services.
3) Observe telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate on default step sizes and window lengths.
4) Gradually flip default to enabled for non-critical namespaces after proven stability.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller scaffolding and reconciler loop implemented.
- [x] API proto changes with migration notes and default values.
- [x] Routing adapter to accept micro-step plans and apply safe rollback hooks.
- [x] Observability (metrics + dashboard) added.
- [x] Integration tests for happy/failure paths.
- [x] Runbook and playbook documented.
- [x] Feature-flag gating implemented for safe initial rollout.

Testing notes:
- Integration tests mock backend saturation and synthetic latency bumps to validate gate behavior.
- Load lab runs with perf-canary show median overhead of the hydrator ~0.3% CPU and negligible added latency (controller runs asynchronously).
- Simulated A/B experiments show reduced incident rate during promotes when hydrator microsteps are used.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly conservative step sizes could prolong rollouts. Mitigation: we provide adaptive step heuristics and an opt-out per-rollout.
- Risk: Misconfigured SLO thresholds may cause spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: we support baseline-relative thresholds and recommend a short observation period before enabling auto-rollback.

Related tickets: ENG-3421 (hydrator prototype), ENG-3490 (rollout telemetry agreement), SUP-7812 (customer incident that motivated micro-step logic).

review_comments: Aisha Patel: This looks good overall. Two asks: (1) add TL;DR on expected operator actions in the runbook, (2) can we expose the observation-window as a rollout-level override?
Author (Marina Lopez): Added operator TL;DR to the top of docs/runbooks/hydrator-playbook.md and made observation_window_ms configurable per-rollout with sane defaults.
Liam Chen: In reconciler.go there was a potential for double-apply when reconcile restarts quickly. Suggest using an in-flight guard keyed by rollout ID.
Author (Marina Lopez): Implemented in-flight guard and added unit tests for concurrent reconcile; clarified comments.
Sofia Martins: Metrics names look good. Add a histogram for step durations and label by rollout cohort to help debugging.
Author (Marina Lopez): Added hydrator_step_duration_seconds histogram and cohort label in metrics exporter.
Aisha Patel: Approving after small nits fixed (docs phrasing).

release_notes: Introduces Traffic Hydrator: opt-in rollout controller to smooth traffic promotes, enforce SLO gates, and trigger automated rollback/playbook actions on gate failures. Feature is disabled by default; enable via rollout.policy.hydrator.enabled. Added metrics, dashboard, and operator runbook.
notes_for_release_engineering: Feature gated. Coordinate canary with platform-team. Ensure observability dashboards are installed in staging before enabling in prod. We recommend enabling on low-traffic namespaces first.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Deploy controller helm chart to staging with feature flag off. 2) Install dashboards. 3) Opt-in 2 internal services for 1 week. 4) Collect telemetry and iterate.
incident_reference: Related to SUP-7812: customer reported repeated backend saturation during large traffic promotes; hydrator addresses this pattern by micro-stepping and SLO-aware fallbacks.
